source.title: Automatic Image-Level Morphological Trait Annotation for Organismal Images
source.authors: Vardaan Pahuja; Samuel Stevens; Alyson East; S. Record; Yu Su

record.tranche_reason: The study uses sparse-autoencoder features as candidate interpretable part detectors, but does not test the listed claims about neuron-pole interpretability rates, held-out explanation accuracy, or causal circuits.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative examples of selected SAE units activating on insect body parts; these bear on neuron interpretability but not on any listed version's specific claim or measure, so they are recorded with versions ["none"]. Human ratings of generated trait descriptions, downstream classification results, and comparisons of annotation methods measure pipeline outcomes rather than neuron interpretability. Values cited from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAE latents (not the model's own neurons) on DINOv2-base as candidate part detectors for a trait-annotation pipeline and evaluates pipeline output quality. It reports no share of interpretable neurons, no held-out or simulation scoring, no InceptionV1 analysis, and no attribution graphs, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SAE latents on DINOv2 features act as spatially grounded, monosemantic candidate part detectors. They use them to build BIOSCAN-Traits (80K traits, 19K images) and report two results: SAE-guided prompting raises expert ratings (3.15 to 3.91), and trait fine-tuning modestly improves BioCLIP zero-shot accuracy. They treat SAE features as a useful decomposition, not the true traits, and filter and validate the resulting annotations.
record.recipe_differences: Uses ReLU sparse autoencoders on DINOv2-base image features and qualitatively inspects selected insect-image activations; it does not perform the Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or held-out explanation evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: Trait-description ratings vary with the number of images per prompt, SAE sparsity and frequency threshold, and MLLM choice; the paper does not report these as changes in neuron interpretability rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected top-activating SAE latents trained on DINOv2-base features of insect images localize to wings, antennae, thorax, leg-body junction, eyes and abdomen (qualitative, hand-picked). The authors also note some latents may merge co-occurring traits.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents on vision foundation-model features can act as spatially localized, part-level detectors on organismal images.

record.problems: Neuron interpretability evidence is qualitative and limited to selected examples; the paper gives no quantitative estimate of the share of interpretable units and no held-out test of whether explanations predict activations. The authors also note that some latents may combine co-occurring traits and that ground-truth morphological annotations are lacking for large-scale evaluation.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or shares of one-job, two-job or unexplained poles.
No cross-model or scale comparison of interpretable-neuron shares.
No analysis of InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose, or recursive generalization versus superposition.
No estimate of the interpretable share of raw neurons by architecture or tool. The SAE sparsity ablation measures trait-description ratings, not neuron interpretability.
No attribution graphs or test of neurons as circuit units against replacement models.
No test of whether activating-example explanations predict activations on held-out data.
No simulation-based automated scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The abstract's claim of 'monosemantic' neurons refers to SAE latents and rests only on hand-picked examples. The paper reports no quantitative monosemanticity measure. The ratings were made by the paper's own authors on 30 samples per configuration.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or estimate of the shares with one job, two related jobs, or unexplained poles.
No comparison of interpretability shares across language models, dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, or model scale up to trillions of parameters.
No analysis of InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron, pose, or recursive generalization versus superposition.
No estimate of the share of interpretable neurons, comparison of tools or architectures for that share, or InceptionV1-sized model estimates.
No attribution graphs or test of whether a model's own neurons explain behavior without a replacement model and its reconstruction error.
No test of explanations against activations not used to write them, or of whether explanations predict where a neuron fires.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.
